summary.en: Women are leading youth-led "Cockroach" protests across India, while the movement's leader was arrested as security forces crack down on demonstrators. In Manipur, a Kuki man was killed, triggering a shutdown that paralysed the Imphal Valley, and subsequent attacks killed three Meitei people, leading to a 48‑hour bandh and the torching of houses in an abandoned village. A scooter rider was killed in a hit-and-run in Jammu and a bus accident in Udhampur killed a girl and a woman, injuring sixteen others. Authorities announced intensified anti-drug operations in Jammu and claimed terrorism is largely curbed in Kashmir. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kvinner leder ungdomsdrevne "Cockroach"‑protester over hele India, mens bevegelsens leder ble arrestert da sikkerhetsstyrker slå ned på demonstranter. I Manipur ble en Kuki-mann drept, noe som utløste en nedstengning som lammet Imphal-dalen, og påfølgende angrep drepte tre Meitei-personer, noe som førte til en 48‑timer lang bandh og brenning av hus i en forlatt landsby. En scooterrytter ble drept i en påkjørsel med flukt i Jammu, og en bussulykke i Udhampur drepte en jente og en kvinne, og 16 andre ble skadet. Myndighetene kunngjorde intensiverte narkotikabekjempelsesoperasjoner i Jammu og hevdet at terrorisme i stor grad er dempet i Kashmir. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
